title: Ghost handoff after TTL expiry caused wrong-model assignment during cross-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a capacity degradation event in eu-west-1 on 2026-03-10 we observed a small percentage of requests getting routed to an incompatible model variant after the routing decision TTL expired. The symptom manifested as higher 5xx rates and degraded output quality for affected customers while the platform simultaneously reported healthy fallback counts. This ticket captures follow-ups and action items from the postmortem to eliminate the ghost-handoff behavior and make detection/mitigation automatic.
incident_summary: At ~2026-03-10T09:12Z increased load and a transient scheduler lag caused routing policy snapshots to be applied with expired TTLs. The fallback orchestration module performed a handoff without re-validating variant compatibility, which produced wrong-variant assignments that then triggered retries and cross-region reroutes, amplifying latency and error amplification for ~12 minutes. Estimated customer impact: 8% of production requests to eu-west-1, several enterprise customers saw degraded completions.
timeline: 2026-03-10T09:08Z - Autoscaler in eu-west-1 began shedding pending pushes due to kernel scheduler contention
2026-03-10T09:12Z - Routing snapshot TTLs expired; fallback orchestrator applied stale snapshot fragments
2026-03-10T09:13Z - First spike in 5xx and latency observed in global dashboards (observability-alert: routing-fallback-errors)
2026-03-10T09:15Z - Canary routing telemetry showed mismatched model flavor tag on 0.7% of requests
2026-03-10T09:18Z - Automated circuit-breaker triggered for eu-west-1, traffic diverted to eu-central and us-west-2 causing cross-region fanout
2026-03-10T09:20Z - Incident declared; mitigation executed to pin routing to last-good snapshot and disable automatic fallback orchestration
2026-03-10T09:24Z - Errors subsided; full traffic normalized by 09:30Z after manual correction of variant compatibility mapping
impact: Errors and high latency for approximately 8% of host requests in eu-west-1 for ~12 minutes. Several enterprise customers reported semantic regressions in generated outputs. No data exfiltration or security breach. Billing impact minimal but SLA exposures for two Dedicated customers possible.
root_cause: Race between routing snapshot TTL expiry and fallback orchestration apply path. The orchestrator assumed that a post-TTL snapshot fragment still carried a compatible variant mapping. There was no final compatibility validation step before assigning the model variant. Additionally, telemetry for mismatched-tags was sampled too coarsely and did not trigger early mitigation.
detection: Alerting was based on aggregate 5xx thresholds which delayed detection until errors rose ~3x baseline. Early signals (variant-tag mismatch counters, per-route quality score drop) were present in telemetry but not wired to automated mitigation.
mitigations_taken: Pinned routing to last-good snapshot for eu-west-1 to stop further handoffs
Disabled automatic fallback orchestration temporarily while we validated mapping rules
Increased sampling of variant-tag telemetry and added an urgent dashboard for per-route flavor-compatibility metrics
Raised circuit-breaker sensitivity for cross-region fanout during high fallback rates
long_term_fix_proposals: Add optimistic-validate step in fallback orchestration: before assigning a variant, verify compatibility matrix and KV cache schema for that request path
Ensure routing snapshot apply is atomic with TTL refresh; introduce snapshot-generation watermark to avoid applying fragments whose TTL is close to expiration
Automatic mitigation hook: if per-route mismatch-rate > 0.1% for 1 minute, immediately roll back to pinned routing and notify SRE/PM
Reduce telemetry sampling window for variant-tag mismatches and wire to bubble-up alerts
Simulate failure mode in canary environments with a synthetic TTL expiry test to validate orchestration behavior

postmortem_notes: Engineering and SRE agreed this is not a one-off; the fallback orchestration code path needs a safety net before model assignment. The compatibility matrix will be extended to include KV cache shape checks and quantization-compatibility flags. PM requests we prioritize user-facing mitigation (automated pin) in the short term. We'll follow up in next retro to align release timing with Dedicated customers' change windows.
